scope: independent narrow readonly review of existing client/backend once-claims, original action flock, primary failure/release handling, and retained exact task cleanup

reviewed_sections.references/android_backend.py: helper root request parser, original global action flock, dispatch call and finally close
reviewed_sections.references/android_app.py: client original protected-production gate, one exact backend spawn, nonzero return propagation and scoped output write
reviewed_sections.source_contract.py: bounded_file, SourceContract manifest/closure verification and private module load

confirmed_properties: Client durable journal mkdir and client.claim are create-only; a repeated client cannot adopt an earlier unknown command. Exact original argv and physical redirect remain bound to the parent intent.
Backend requires the actually recorded client request and dispatch digest, then creates its own backend.claim before calling the pinned original helper; no replay branch is present.
Only the private backend module arun is replaced. The original helper still acquires the same global action flock before dispatch and closes it in finally.

The bound transport records the actual command observation before entry lease release, retains a primary command failure through release/postguard/evidence failures, and permanently poisons that transport after a failure.

If backend close or final result publication fails after helper success, the backend returns nonzero and the original client propagates it before forwarding success stdout. A release error cannot make an earlier failure green.

Flow.cleanup has exactly the same Python AST as the frozen original recorder: preserves preexisting tasks, uses the original selected task scope, takes the original action lock, durably marks one removal attempt, checks exact leaf, then verifies removal and other-task preservation.
limitations: No independent execution of the existing 42 controls in this review.
This is not a whole-wrapper or shared namespace helper qualification.
The r1 main_classpaths release-error issue is outside this narrow scope; parent/owner reported its separate r2 fix.
Action-runner APK qualification, actual UI requests, app reopen/audio and whole-app production readiness remain open.
